Let's break down the question: It asks what we know will happen to gold in the next twenty years, given that it has gone up in value over the last twenty years.

Option A ("Gold will go down") is not justified; past performance does not guarantee a reversal.
Option B ("We know prices will rise") is also not justified; we cannot know this for certain.
Option C ("Gold could either rise or fall in value") is a true statement—past performance does not guarantee future results, and the price could go either way.
Option D ("If gold has gone up in value over the last twenty years, it will rise in the next twenty years") is not justified; there is no certainty.
Option E ("If gold has gone up in value over the last twenty years, it will keep going up") is also not justified.
Option F ("Gold keeps going up") is not justified.
Option G ("Gold values will stay the same") is not justified.
Option H ("Nothing") is a bit ambiguous, but it could be interpreted as "we know nothing about the future," which is close to correct, but not as precise as Option C.

Option C is the best answer because it accurately reflects the uncertainty of future price movements, regardless of past trends.

Answer: C
